XPENG shows a unisex IRON with VLA 3.0 and targets January 2027 production

A live demonstration confirms the planned body design and retail trial roadmap, while conversation still shows rough edges.

Humanoids Daily ↗25 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 4Videos 1

The planned production design

At its November 25 AI Day, XPENG showed IRON and confirmed one unisex design, replacing earlier male and female options. The robot has 76 degrees of freedom and more than 1,500 tactile points. Reporting from the event describes walking, microphone handling and interaction near attendees.

Architecture and demonstration limits

XPENG describes VLA 3.0 as three loops for planning, immediate response and hardware execution, supported by three Turing chips totaling 2,250 TOPS. These are company-presented specifications. Live conversation still included unexpected language switching and questions directed back at journalists, limiting conclusions about readiness for general service work.

Production and delivery targets

Production is targeted for January 2027, with sales and tour-guide trials in XPENG stores during the first quarter and commercial release and external deliveries in the second. One unit every 2.5 minutes is the line’s designed full-capacity rate, not current achieved output. Pricing remains unannounced.
